titre: Mario Kart World Officially Adds New Courses, Fan Requested Features
chapo: Mario Kart World just got a free update with new courses and more.
extrait: To no one’s surprise, Mario Kart World remains the best-selling game on the Nintendo Switch 2, with an impressive 16.48 million copies sold. When you consider that there are only around 26.35 million Switch 2 owners total, that means almost 63 percent of Switch 2 players have a copy of Mario’s latest kart racer. It's a somewhat staggering figure, given that the game costs $79.99. Now, more than a year after its release, Nintendo is bringing new courses and fan-requested features to the Switch launch game. Nintendo released the latest update for Mario Kart World on Tuesday, and players have responded to it well. Ver 1.9.0 is a free update that adds eight remixed tracks, among other changes. The updated courses use a somewhat hilarious naming convention of slapping a 2 onto the end of each stage name. As a Redditor explained, there are basically three types of course remixes included: reverse variants, entirely new track layouts, and an existing path made into its own track. Specifically, Salty Salty Speedway 2, Mario Bros Circuit 2, and Airship Fortress 2 are new tracks with reused assets; DK Pass 2, Wario Stadium 2, Desert Hills 2, and Koopa Troopa Beach 2 are reverse variants; and Shy Guy Bazaar 2 turns an existing path into its own track. Beyond the remixed courses, the update also adds two new routes for Knockout Tour mode, in which racers compete until only one is left standing. There’s Feather Rally, which connects Mario Bros Circuit to Boo Cinema, and Lucky Cat Rally, which links Question Block Ruins to Sky-High Sunday. Lastly, 1.9.0 brings an enhanced Replay feature that lets you view past races and battles, so you can relive that time you were in first until you got hit by a blue shell, Bullet Bill, and a lightning bolt. Unlike some of Mario Kart World’s updates, fans have responded well to the game’s latest patch. “This was a great update and adds more variety to the game’s track selection while being free DLC. I actually can’t wait to see more for it,” one Redditor wrote. Another user commented, “This is a great format for an update- 8 new tracks (with a combination of reverse and new layouts) and 2 new tour rallies. They should have been doing this every 3 or 4 months after release, in my opinion.” Despite Mario Kart World’s impressive sales figures and generally positive reviews, the game has divided its player base due to certain design decisions. titre: La mise à jour 1.9.0 de Mario Kart World vient de sortir sur Switch 2, mais quand est-ce qu’on retrouve les vraies courses en 3 tours ?
chapo: Nintendo vient de remettre une pièce dans la machine Mario Kart World, et il y a de quoi faire. Sauf qu’il manque toujours le truc que tout le monde réclame depuis la sortie.
extrait: 🚨 Black Friday : RDV le 27 novembre 2026 à 17h00 pour tenter de gagner +3700€ de cadeaux 🎁 Nintendo vient de remettre une pièce dans la machine Mario Kart World, et il y a de quoi faire. Sauf qu’il manque toujours le truc que tout le monde réclame depuis la sortie. Depuis son lancement avec la Switch 2, Mario Kart World a droit à des mises à jour régulières, et gratuites. Nouveaux réglages, corrections de bugs, ajustements des objets… Nintendo suit son jeu de près, c’est indéniable. Par contre, un sujet revient en boucle à chaque patch dans les commentaires et sur les réseaux, et Nintendo semble toujours ignorer la grogne des fans. On a donc jeté un oeil aux notes de la version 1.9.0. Le gros morceau, ce sont huit circuits remixés à partir de tracés existants : Mario Bros. Circuit 2, Desert Hills 2, Shy Guy Bazaar 2, Wario Stadium 2, Airship Fortress 2, DK Pass 2, Koopa Troopa Beach 2 et Salty Salty Speedway 2. Le mode Survie récupère aussi deux nouveaux rallyes (Feather Rally et Lucky Cat Rally), et un menu Replay fait enfin son apparition pour revoir ses courses et batailles, sauvegardées automatiquement. Le reste tient du peaufinage : les missions des interrupteurs P deviennent accessibles en Balade en ligne, le mode spectateur affiche désormais l’objet du joueur suivi, les probabilités de certains objets sont revues et une bonne quinzaine de bugs passent à la trappe. Rien de honteux, donc, et la mise à jour reste la bienvenue. Mais soyons honnêtes, des variantes de circuits qu’on connaît déjà, ça ne remplace pas de vrais nouveaux circuits ou de nouveaux pilotes, et c’est surtout ça que les joueurs attendent maintenant. En ligne, la plupart des courses passent toujours par ces fameuses intermissions, où l’on roule surtout sur les routes qui relient deux circuits avant de ne faire qu’un seul tour du tracé final. Au lancement, les joueurs avaient trouvé une parade : choisir l’option Aléatoire, qui proposait presque à chaque fois une course classique en 3 tours. Nintendo y a mis fin en ajoutant les intermissions dans le tirage Aléatoire. Le patch 1.2.0 a ensuite rendu les courses en 3 tours un peu plus fréquentes, mais certains joueurs estimaient qu’on ne les voyait toujours que 20 à 30 % du temps. Un an et demi plus tard, la 1.9.0 ne change rien. Il n’y a toujours aucune option pour jouer en ligne uniquement en 3 tours, Nintendo ignorant les demandes de sa communauté ici. titre: Mario Kart World patch adds 8 new tracks – but they're all sequels to Nintendo's old maps
chapo: 1.9.0 races in with new Knockout Tour routes, too
extrait: By submitting your information you agree to the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy and are aged 16 or over. Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox. Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards. Mario Kart World just got a massive new update in version 1.9.0, finally bringing Nintendo's Switch 2 racing game into the limelight – but not all fans are satisfied. Nintendo unveils 1.9.0 in a colorful trailer on YouTube, featuring eight "new" tracks and two Knockout Tour routes – and yes, the quote marks around the word "new" are intentional on my part. That's because the tracks are sequels of sorts, acting as the "two" counterparts to already existing maps: Airship Fortress 2, Desert Hills 2, DK Pass 2, Maio Bros. Circuit 2, Koopa Troopa Beach 2, Salty Salty Speedway 2, and Wario Stadium 2. Fans are jokingly calling 1.9.0 the "update of 2s" in the comments, noting that there isn't one truly new map in the lineup here. They're just reverse takes on old tracks, really. "This update certainly has 'The Power of Two' in it," reads one reply. Another jests, "This is like if McDonald's slapped a McChicken inside a McDouble, put it in a new box, and called it a brand-new menu item," clarifying they're "not mad at this update, though." There is still 2.0 to look forward to, after all – and players note that's likely why Nintendo hasn't dropped anything too big in 1.9.0. "People don't seem to realize we're getting close to a 2.0 update," as one response puts it. "That's the big one that will have a lot of stuff that probably people are looking for and stuff that people aren't expecting." As for the Knockout Tour routes, this week's patch also brings two: Feather Rally and Lucky Cat Rally. The new version includes plenty of other changes, as outlined on Nintendo's official support website. They range from technical to wholesome, like the fact that "confetti now falls during the results presentation in Grand Prix and Knockout Tour." Folks can also now pass through the river route to Cheep Cheep Falls from DK Pass, Sky-High Sundae, Salty Salty Speedway, Starview Peak, and Wario Shipyard. All in all, it's not a bad update – heck, at least it's something seeing the love Nintendo's given Mario Kart 8 recently – but it does leave ample room for a banger 2.0, if you ask me.
